in expert judgment, the 'full signal' is unobservable and must be inferred from outcome data.","The checklist may encode cues the expert does not use (if authored by a different expert or crowd), making the checklist a different estimator, not a compression."],"overturn_conditions":["If the panel and expert do not diverge on expert-unique items, either the checklist is complete (panel dominates) or the expert's unique cues are irrelevant (no test).","If the checklist encodes cues no expert uses and outperforms, the compression frame is overturned and a different mechanism is needed."],"shared_structure":["Both frame the comparison as compression vs. original: the checklist is a compressed version of expert judgment, and compression is lossy with respect to configural cues.","Both identify the test case as one where the omitted information is outcome-relevant, not merely where the overall accuracy differs.","Both predict that the panel and expert diverge specifically on cases requiring the omitted information, not uniformly across all cases."],"source_memory_refs":["SRC_006","SRC_007","SCR_001"],"transfer_claims":["The conditional superiority transfers: panel>expert only when compression loss is immaterial to the outcome distribution.","The diagnostic (divergence on expert-unique, outcome-determinative items) transfers as the within-evaluation evidence."]},"claim":"The panel's superiority is contingent on the checklist encoding the dominant cues the expert uses; the decisive evidence is a divergence between panel and expert specifically on items where an expert-unique cue is outcome-determinative, revealing whether the checklist has merely tracked the easy cases or genuinely captured the expert's cue-set.","counterconditions":[{"case":"If the expert does not actually use any unique cues (the checklist is a complete specification), there is no divergence to detect and the panel dominates unconditionally.","checker_spec":null,"eval":"observation"},{"case":"If the expert's unique cues are never outcome-determinative in the evaluation sample, the divergence cannot be observed in a single evaluation.","checker_spec":null,"eval":"observation"},{"case":"If the checklist is crowd-evolved rather than expert-authored, the 'lossy compression' mechanism fails: the checklist may contain cues no single expert uses.","checker_spec":null,"eval":"observation"}],"definitions":[],"derivation":[],"formalization_refs":[],"mechanism":"The checklist is a lossy compression of the expert's cue-set: it transmits the most salient, articulable cues but may omit configural or tacit cues the expert uses implicitly. The panel outperforms the expert on average only when the omitted cues are rarely outcome-determinative. Genuine reliability gain is distinguished from coincidental compliance by examining cases where an expert-unique cue (a cue the expert uses but the checklist omits) is the deciding factor: if the panel tracks the right answer even on these items, the checklist has captured the generative structure; if the panel fails specifically and systematically on these items, the gain is merely compliance on easy cases.","premises":[],"schema":"deepreason-reasoning-envelope-v1","scope":{"covers":[],"excludes":[]},"simulation_refs":[],"uncertainties":[]}
